source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Wheels and Tires, p.10-4

procedures.title: Tire wear: diagnose
steps: Cornering also overloads and distorts the outside tires, wearing their outer half like excess positive camber.
Tell cornering wear from camber wear by the rounded outer shoulder and roughened, abraded tread; it may leave a fin along each tread row or a stepped look.
The only cure for cornering wear is gentler driving.

procedures.title: Tires: rotate
steps: Rotate tires every 6000 miles, or sooner with heavy wear; Corvette tires every 4000 miles or sooner.
Follow the pattern in figure 5 of the manual (a 5-wheel pattern that brings the spare into use, or a 4-wheel pattern in which the fronts move straight back and the rears cross to the opposite front).
While the tires are off, look for unusual wear and bulges, and remove stones, glass and nails.
Reset front and rear pressures per the inflation table in Specifications, Section 10.
notes: Following the schedule gives every tire equal mileage in each position by the end of the fourth change.

procedures.title: Tire noise: diagnose
steps: Drive at various speeds under part throttle, hard acceleration and deceleration: axle and exhaust noise change with these conditions, tire noise does not.
Drive a smooth stretch at normal pressure, then again with tires at fifty pounds; tire noise drops noticeably, axle noise does not.
Lower the tires back to normal one at a time to find the noisy one; never leave the high pressure in after the test.
If the front tires make most of the noise, check front wheel alignment.
notes: Tire noise is loudest at about 20-30 mph.
Common causes: pressure below recommendation, misalignment, uneven wear, or a defective (thumper) tire.

procedures.title: Tires: clean
steps: Sponge off road dirt with clear water or mild soap solution.
For whitewalls, a good whitewall cleaner works faster and removes stains soap will not.
notes: Never use gasoline, kerosene or any petroleum-based cleaner: oil damages and discolors tire rubber.

procedures.title: Road wheel: change with jack
steps: Apply the parking brake; block the front wheels when changing a rear.
Take off the hub cap or wheel disc and break the wheel nuts loose.
Position the jack as described in Section 0 (General Information) and lift until the tire is off the ground.
Remove the nuts and the wheel.
Reinstall in reverse order and torque the nuts to 55-75 ft. lbs.
notes: Caution: with wheel discs, line up the disc's pilot hole with the valve stem so its anti-rotation notches engage the lugs on the rim.

procedures.title: Tires: repair punctures
steps: After a tire has lost all or most of its air, especially at highway speed, dismount it and inspect inside for damage.
